purpose: Malicious adapter ids that must be rejected by the static registry BEFORE any process is created. Each is an opaque string to the runner; none is split, interpolated, or passed to a shell. Every entry must raise UnknownAdapterError(CONTRACT_INVALID) at get_adapter, so no subprocess is ever spawned for it.

cases.notes: Classic injection attempt. The registry does a plain dict lookup; this id is not a key, so it is rejected. The id is never placed in a shell string.
Would fetch and execute a remote payload under naive shell invocation. The runner uses no shell; the id is rejected at lookup.

cases.vector: path traversal as an adapter id
cases.notes: The registry is not a filesystem; this is an unknown key and is rejected. There is no path that the id resolves against.
No shell evaluates the backticks; the id is rejected at lookup.
No shell evaluates the substitution; the id is rejected at lookup.
No pipe is constructed; the id is rejected at lookup.
A newline in the id does not start a new command; the id is a single rejected key.

cases.vector: SQL-injection-style payload (irrelevant to the registry, but representative of fuzz input)
cases.notes: The registry is not a query; the id is rejected at lookup.
